intro.say: Shapes can join together to make pictures, like a house!

rounds.say: Put a triangle on top of a square and you have a house! The triangle is the roof.
Stack circles on top of each other and you can make a snowman!

rounds.ask: Which shape makes the roof of the house?

options.why: A star has too many points for a roof.
A circle is round, but a roof is pointy.

rounds.explain: A triangle has a pointy top, just like a roof.

options.why: Two circles make a snowman.
Stars don't make walls and a roof.

rounds.explain: A triangle roof on a square makes a house.

rounds.ask: What shape do we stack to make a snowman?

options.why: Triangles are pointy, but snowballs are round.
A snowman is round, not square.

rounds.explain: Snowballs are round, so a snowman is made of circles.

rounds.ask: A circle on top of a long thin rectangle. What did we build?

options.label: house
options.why: A house needs a triangle roof.

options.label: star
options.why: A star has five points.

rounds.explain: A round circle on a thin stick makes a lollipop!

rounds.ask: An ice cream is a circle on top of which shape?

options.why: The cone is pointy, not a heart.
The cone gets thin and pointy.

rounds.explain: The cone is a triangle, with the scoop of ice cream on top.

intro.say: Two shapes can join together to make a brand new shape!

rounds.say: Cut a square from corner to corner and you get two triangles. Put them back together and you have a square again!
rounds.caption: 2 triangles make a square

rounds.say: Put two squares side by side and they make a long rectangle.
rounds.caption: 2 squares make a rectangle

rounds.ask: A square was cut corner to corner into two triangles. Put them back together. What shape is it?

options.why: Triangles have straight sides, so they can't make a circle.
Two triangles can't make all those points.

rounds.explain: The two triangles fit back together to make the square.

rounds.ask: Two squares side by side make which shape?

options.why: Squares make straight, long shapes, not pointy ones.
Squares have straight sides, so they can't make a circle.

rounds.explain: Two squares in a row make a long rectangle.

rounds.ask: How many small squares make this big square?

options.why: Count the top row and the bottom row.
Count each small square just once.

rounds.explain: Two on top and two on the bottom make 4 small squares.

rounds.ask: Which shapes would make this tree?

options.why: A tree like this is pointy on top.
Look for a pointy top and a trunk.

rounds.explain: A triangle on top of a small brown square makes a tree.

rounds.ask: Does the picture use a circle?
rounds.explain: Wheels and snowmen use circles. Houses, trees and the triangle ruler don't.

intro.say: Let's solve shape puzzles! Count the pieces and work out what they build.

rounds.say: Six triangles fit together around a middle point to make a hexagon!
rounds.caption: 6 triangles make a hexagon

rounds.say: A robot is built from shapes: a square head, a rectangle body, and rectangle arms and legs.
rounds.caption: shapes make pictures

rounds.ask: Two triangles make one square. How many triangles make two squares?

options.why: That only makes one square.
Each square needs 2 triangles.

rounds.explain: Each square needs 2 triangles, and 2 and 2 make 4.

rounds.ask: How many small squares are in this rectangle?

options.why: Count the top row and the bottom row.
Count each square only once.

rounds.explain: There are 2 rows of 3 squares, which makes 6.
rounds.hint: Count the top row, then keep counting.

rounds.ask: Each house uses 1 triangle and 1 square. How many shapes make 3 houses?

options.why: Each house needs 2 shapes.
Count 2 shapes for each house.

rounds.explain: Each house uses 2 shapes, so 3 houses use 2, 4, 6 shapes.

rounds.ask: Which shape can you NOT make from two squares?

options.why: Two squares side by side do make a rectangle.

rounds.explain: Squares have straight sides, so they can never make a round circle.

rounds.ask: The robot has 1 square head, 1 rectangle body and 4 rectangles for arms and legs. How many shapes in all?

options.why: Count the head, the body and all 4 limbs.
Count again: 1 and 1 and 4.

rounds.explain: One head, one body and four limbs make 6 shapes.

rounds.ask: A big square is made of 4 small squares. You take 1 away. How many small squares are left?

options.why: Only one square was taken away.
One square was taken away.

rounds.explain: Four squares take away one leaves 3.
